`tensor_diffs` must contain one entry per tensor name present in either checkpoint, sorted lexicographically by tensor name.

behavior_constraints: NOT is a prefix operator with highest precedence, so `NOT epoch == 0` excludes all epoch-0 entries.
AND binds tighter than OR.
Parentheses override default precedence; `(step < 5 OR step > 95) AND epoch == 0` must group the OR first then apply AND.
`loss > 1.0 OR NOT grad_norm > 5.0 AND epoch == 3` parses as `loss > 1.0 OR ((NOT (grad_norm > 5.0)) AND epoch == 3)`.
Malformed parenthesized queries such as `(step < 5` or `step < 5)` must exit non-zero with an error message on stderr.
The grammar must follow: query := or_expr; or_expr := and_expr ("OR" and_expr)*; and_expr := not_expr ("AND" not_expr)*; not_expr := "NOT" not_expr | atom; atom := "(" or_expr ")" | condition.
Supported fields remain step, epoch, loss, lr, grad_norm, acc, event, ts.
Comparison operators remain >, <, >=, <=, ==, !=.
All existing query syntax must continue to work after the changes.

behavior_constraints: Severity levels are exactly five: critical, high, medium, low, info (most to least severe).
tensor_checksum_mismatch, header_checksum_mismatch, and signature_invalid anomalies are classified critical.
loss_divergence is critical when increase ratio > 5.0, otherwise high.
gradient_spike is high when z-score > 5.0, otherwise medium.
metric_regression and dataset_hash_inconsistency are high.
provenance_chain_break is medium.
lr_anomaly is info.
training_gap is info.
Anomalies are sorted by severity rank, then type alphabetically, then epoch ascending, then step ascending.
detect.summary.by_severity includes a count for each severity present in the returned anomaly list, including an info key when info-level anomalies are returned.

Update `/app/docs/analysis_rules.md`, `/app/docs/output_schema.md`, and the implementation for the reworked anomaly severity classification system. The existing docs may not contain these changes yet, so use the contract below.

The previous 4-level system (`critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`) is replaced with a 5-level system that adds an `info` level for non-actionable observations.

Severity order, from most severe to least severe, is:

```text
critical > high > medium > low > info
```

behavior_constraints: Gradient spike detection uses EWMA (alpha=0.1) over grad_norm values in timeline order, tracking EWMA mean and EWMA variance.
Gradient spike detection requires a minimum warmup of 30 entries before any anomaly is emitted.
Gradient spike is triggered when EWMA-based z_score > 2.5.
Gradient spike severity is high when z_score > 4.0, otherwise medium.
Gradient spike anomaly details object includes observed (current grad_norm), ewma_mean, ewma_stddev (sqrt of EWMA variance), and z_score.
Loss divergence detection uses EMA (alpha=0.05) over loss values in timeline order instead of comparing window endpoints.
Loss divergence is triggered when current_loss > 2.0 * ema_loss.
Loss divergence detection is suppressed when abs(ema_loss) <= 1e-6.
Loss divergence severity is critical when current_loss / ema_loss > 5.0, otherwise high.
Loss divergence anomaly details object includes current_loss, ema_loss, and ratio (current_loss / ema_loss).
